title: Charcoal Briquettes 8kg

drivers.name: 20% off promotion
drivers.evidence: Deeper than most past promotions (max 30% off). One 30% off saw 2.53x lift; one 25% off on holiday saw 4.58x lift. Noise-adjusted average lift is x1.0, but this event is likely stronger due to heatwave. Adjusted for depth and context.

drivers.name: Heatwave forecast (38°C)
drivers.evidence: High heat drives grilling demand. No direct past heatwave data, but summer spikes (e.g., Labor Day) show 2.7x lift. This is a new driver with plausible impact, but limited evidence. Add 30% as a conservative uplift.

adjustment.analysis: The 20% discount is deeper than past promotions (max 30% off, but only one such event). The 2026-06-29 25% off during Independence Day drove a 4.58x lift, suggesting strong demand elasticity. However, the 2026-04-06 30% off also saw a 2.53x lift, but this was isolated. The noise-adjusted average lift from past promotions is x1.0, indicating most promotions had little effect. The current week has a heatwave (38°C), which historically correlates with higher grilling demand. The baseline is trending downward (trend_13_vs_prior_13_pct = -32.2%), but the heatwave and promotion may offset this. The classical model's x1.0 is too low; we adjust upward for the promotion and heatwave, but shrink due to thin evidence and potential overfit. The heatwave is a new driver with no prior overlap, so we treat it as an independent uplift. The past promotion lifts are inconsistent, so we apply moderate confidence.

  median 28.3 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 74.0 | 10%-90%: 5.9 - 51.8

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-73% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
